shots.label: 1 — Choosing a story
shots.prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural.
Generate one NEW candid family snapshot for a Hey Kahani landing-page hero, wide 16:9. The goal is an unposed believable everyday moment observed by someone in the room.
Reference 1 is ONLY for the boy's identity (five-year-old South Asian boy, short wavy brown hair, freckles, cream/peach checked cotton shirt) and the cream/peach/oak color family. Completely replace its posed hands, symmetrical product arrangement, stiff posture and catalog framing. Reference 2 is ONLY the Player design: rounded cream cylinder, arch carry handle, five embossed cream controls in cross layout, lower red woven speaker band, light wood base.
Exactly one child and one compact Player. Three SMALL circular illustrated Koel story tokens. Sensible real-world relative scale: Player body narrower than his face, total height including handle approximately his head height. Koels are much smaller than a child's palm, about half the Player's diameter. Natural small child hands, short fingers, slender wrists, believable arm lengths. Child, hands and product are in the same depth plane so perspective cannot inflate the hands or objects.
Photographic treatment: a parent quietly took an excellent natural-light snapshot during ordinary play. Soft mixed window light with gentle real shadow falloff, neutral believable skin tones, slightly imperfect exposure, understated cotton weave and little shirt wrinkles, a few flyaway hairs. Warm daylight without orange filter, glossy skin, soft-focus beauty retouching or CGI surfaces. Real physical contact, weight and table shadows. No studio key/fill setup, no theatrical light beams. No forced smile. The child is absorbed in the action and unaware of the camera.
Simple lived-in family breakfast nook with oak table, pale peach wall, cream bench. A lightly rumpled cushion and ordinary small marks in the wood are enough: keep clutter minimal. The composition should feel found, casually asymmetrical and a little off-center; no neatly staged line of discs or child presenting product. Keep some quieter space toward the left for page copy without making a blank gradient void.
No second person, phone/tablet, text, logos, watermarks, collage or UI. No oversized Player, large coaster-size tokens, giant adult hands, extra fingers or elongated arms. Generate a new natural pose from the action below; do not just rearrange the fingers of the reference.
Moment: a child caught in the middle of choosing, rather than smiling for a product photo. The boy is kneeling sideways on the bench with one knee folded underneath him, leaning toward the table naturally. His right fingertips are sliding ONE little Koel along the tabletop toward the Player. The other hand supports his weight on the bench edge, not posed on the product. Two other Koels lie at uneven distances, one partly hidden behind the Player. He looks down with a thoughtful almost-smile and slightly parted lips. Normal 50mm perspective from the opposite corner of the table, child-eye-height medium environmental view. His arms are relaxed, tabletop close to his torso. Show the spontaneous forward lean and naturally wrinkled shirt; no formal portrait posture.
